fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency equipment can reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Create a turnaround area near the residence or detached structure large enough for a fire engine or ambulance to reverse direction without backing out to the road.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation that crowds the edges of the access drive to allow full vehicle width passage.
• Thin or remove dense vegetation growing directly against the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around the exterior of both buildings.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without pushing through vegetation.
• If a gate controls the single access point, keep it unlocked or install a Knox Box or standard emergency access lock so responders are not delayed at the entrance.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Brush Area
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or overhanging the house.
• Clear ground vegetation, grass, and leaf litter within the immediate area surrounding the house.
• Thin the tree clusters near the house so branches no longer touch or overlap each other.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees closest to the house, working outward from the walls.
• Separate the scattered shrubs from the base of the house by removing or relocating those growing against the structure.
• Cut back the brush area to create open ground between it and the nearest structure.
• Thin the scattered trees near the house so they stand individually with open space between their canopies.
• Remove dead wood, fallen branches, and accumulated debris from beneath trees near the house.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation along the full length of the driveway to keep it passable.
• Maintain clear, open ground directly around the house so a person can walk completely around it without pushing through vegetation.
• Cut back the brush area nearest to the house so it does not form a continuous path of vegetation leading to the structure.
